title: Marrero's method book and teaching banjo as a chord instrument
summary: Marrero used a method book; Guesnon teaches chords and counting rather than single notes and criticizes other local teachers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: In regard to John, I keep pumping you about John Marrero. Oh, he's way pumping about, I tell you.
Hardly any of the Marrero's left to talk for themselves. So, did he use a method, any kind of a book?
Yeah, Arthur Black. Arthur Black Methods. That's the first method he got me to teach you.
Did you have any other music? Did he write out pieces for you?

Oh, yeah. Well, yeah. Well, you see, everything I do today is practically what he done for me. You see, because I've been having a few students coming to me from different schools around here. You tell them make C, they make the note of C. You see, make A, they make the note of A. Whoever is teaching them is going about the wrong way. Now, if you had a violin pupil, that would be right. Because a violin is a note instrument. But the banjo is a chord instrument. So, what you want to learn a man to do, you want to learn him how to count one, two, three, four beats to the measure. You want to learn him how to make the chord of A7. Or the chord of D minor. Not the note of D. Or the chord of F. And that's the whole trouble. I don't know how they're teaching them. But, I mean, if that's their way, they would spend... Well, in fact, I got a boy right now, Ivory Foster. He's been taking lessons nine months out here from some teacher. And he come in the house and he can't make the chord of C. I mean, that's just one of them things. I mean, you know, in other words... Well, I mean, a lot of my... That's a very good friend of mine. No name called. I told him, I said... Man, I said, you got a guy. I said, you a saxophone player. I said, and you teaching so-and-so guitar. I said, and every time I look, you watching my fingers to see what chord I'm making. So you go back and show that to somebody else. I said, man, I don't think you're going to make the greatest of guitar teacher. He said, well, my conception is, man, I don't care if the cat learned or not. All I want is the $2. Well, you see, with me, it ain't like that. If a guy come to me and he can't learn something in two weeks, I said, look, man, I'll come back.
